newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnia to sign debt deal with London club - official.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia to sign debt deal with London club - official.

text.p: Bosnia is expected to sign a debt deal with London club creditors on Monday at the U.S. embassy in Sarajevo, government officials said.
Bosnia finished negotiations on Monday on restructuring a $1.04 billion debt with commercial bank creditors, a Western banking official in Sarajevo said.
Bosnia has assumed responsibility for $404 million of the $1.04 billion sum, while the remainder has been taken over by other former Yugoslav republics, the official said.

Of the $404 million, Bosnia is to pay $150 million at a favorable rate over an initial seven-year grace period. In the first five years the interest rate will be two percent, in the following two years the rate would be three percent.
After the seven-year period, the interest rate rises to 3.5 percent until the tenth year.
After ten years, the interest rate will be Libor (London Inter Bank Offered Rate) plus 0.825 percent, the source said.
The second part of the debt, which amounts to $254 million, will not be paid until the country's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) per capita rises to $2,500, indexed to German inflation from 1997.
"When this becomes a case, the amount will be amortized in equal payments over 12 years at the same Libor and 0.825 percent rate," he said.
"So if you put all this together, Bosnia got a very good debt reduction of 87.5 percent, which is one of the best," he said.
Bosnia, which began debt talks with the London Club of commercial bank creditors last Wednesday, had asked for 90 percent forgiveness.
A signing ceremony was scheduled later on Monday at the U.S embassy in Sarajevo, information ministry officials said.
"The signing is there because the biggest creditor is Chase Manhattan, which was also the chair of the committee representing creditors," the source said.
